To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the transport capacity of a wireless network is no more than the transport capacity of its underlying undirected graph (b) the transport capacity can be attained through a multihope strategy that is independent of the channel states.

(a) the capacity of a network of nodes is no more than n, even when all channel state information is noncausally available; (b) the capacity of an n-node network is O(n) if all channels are independent and frequency selective; and (c) the capacity of the network is O(1) if there are no more than n/2 nodes.

the transport capacity of fading networks is O(n), even if the channel states are noncausally and perfectly known, and is achievable with a multihop routing strategy, even when the channel is frequency selective and time-varying.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental limits of communication over wireless networks.
the design of wireless communication networks.
the design of wireless networks that can be deployed with a-priori channel state information (CSI).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transport capacity of a wireless network is at most logarithmic in the number of nodes, and that it is achieved by multihop communication.
in fading channels, the transport capacity of a wireless network is O(G(n)).
the transport capacity of a wireless network is at most logarithmic in the number of nodes, and that this bound is achievable through the use of a multihop protocol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in fading networks, the transport capacity of a network of n users is at best O(n) and at most O(n^2).
the transport capacity of a wireless network is no more than G(n), and that G(n) can be achieved even in the presence of frequency-selective channels and fading.
in the high attenuation setting the transport capacity of a wireless network is at most logarithmic in the size of the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the class of networks considered, the transport capacity scales linearly in the number of nodes and is independent of the channel statistics.
the high attenuation regime is not as limiting as it is usually thought to be.
the transport capacity of fading networks is no better than that of noise-limited networks.
